experiences.name: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Portugal's soulful Fado music tradition with an intimate dinner at a traditional Fado house in the historic Alfama district. Enjoy authentic petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local wine, and live Fado performances by seasoned musicians in a centuries-old setting.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Time Out Market, a curated food hall showcasing the best of Lisbon's culinary scene. Sample iconic dishes including bacalhau (salted cod), pastéis de nata (custard tarts), piri-piri chicken, and local cheeses from award-winning chefs and vendors all under one roof.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Tour of Belém Historic District
experiences.description: Discover Lisbon's Age of Discovery heritage with a guided walking tour of Belém. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, the iconic Tower of Belém, and the Monument to the Discoveries. Learn about Portugal's maritime history and its global impact from the 15th century onward.

experiences.name: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Exploration
experiences.description: Visit the medieval Castelo de São Jorge perched atop Lisbon's highest hill, offering panoramic city views and archaeological ruins dating back to the Moorish era. Afterward, wander through the multicultural Mouraria neighborhood, Lisbon's oldest district, exploring its narrow streets, local taverns, and vibrant street art.

experiences.name: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Brunch
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely Sunday morning at the LX Factory, a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex transformed into a creative hub. Browse artisan stalls, vintage shops, and local food vendors. Enjoy a traditional Portuguese brunch featuring fresh bread, local cheeses, charcuterie, and freshly brewed coffee in a bohemian atmosphere.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Time Out Market, a curated food hall showcasing the best of Lisbon's culinary scene. Sample iconic dishes including bacalhau (salted cod), pastéis de nata (custard tarts), piri-piri chicken, and local cheeses from award-winning chefs and vendors all under one roof.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Tour of Belém Historic District
experiences.description: Discover Lisbon's Age of Discovery heritage with a guided walking tour of Belém. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, the iconic Tower of Belém, and the Monument to the Discoveries. Learn about Portugal's maritime history and its global impact from the 15th century onward.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line) from the airport to central Lisbon for around €1.85–€2.00. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's historic downtown. Walk along Rua Augusta, pass through the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta (free exterior viewing), and explore Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River — all free and within easy reach of most central accommodations.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Alfama district for your first taste of authentic Lisbon. Wander the narrow medieval streets, catch a glimpse of São Jorge Castle lit up at night, and soak in the atmosphere of the oldest neighborhood in the city.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastel de nata (custard tart) and a bica (espresso) at a local café near the airport or hotel for under €2 — a classic Portuguese welcome.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bifana (pork sandwich) or prego (beef sandwich) from a local tasca or street counter in Baixa for €2–€4.
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional tasca in Alfama. Look for a prato do dia (daily special) which typically includes soup, a main course, bread, and a drink for €8–€12. Try bacalhau à brás (shredded salted cod with eggs and fries) as your first proper Portuguese meal.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a rechargeable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (€0.50 card fee) and load it with credit for all public transport. Avoid taxis from the airport — Metro or Aerobus is far cheaper. Keep your first evening relaxed as jet lag or travel fatigue may set in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Castelo de São Jorge (São Jorge Castle) when it opens. Arrive early to beat crowds. Entry is €15 for adults but check for discounts with a Lisbon Card or look for free entry days. Enjoy panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River from the battlements. Explore the Moorish and medieval history of this hilltop fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — an ideal way to explore Lisbon's culinary scene on a budget while learning about local food culture. The iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré brings together the best chefs and producers in the city. Even without a formal tour, you can graze affordably by sharing small dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bairro Alto neighborhood as it comes alive in the evening. Browse the bohemian streets, pop into local wine bars for a glass of vinho verde or ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and enjoy the vibrant nightlife atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local padaria (bakery) near your hotel for a galão (milky coffee) and a torrada (toasted bread with butter) for under €3.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Time Out Market — share two or three small plates between yourself or try a single hearty dish. Budget €10–€15 for a satisfying lunch with a drink.
meals.dinner: Head to a no-frills tasca in Bairro Alto for a simple grilled fish (peixe grelhado) or carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams). Look for restaurants with handwritten menus outside — a sign of authenticity and value. Budget €10–€13 including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market is busiest on weekends — go at opening time (10:00) or after 14:00 to avoid the largest crowds. Ginjinha is best enjoyed at A Ginjinha near Rossio Square for just €1.40 a shot — a beloved local tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Guided Walking Tour of Belém Historic District to discover Lisbon's Age of Discovery heritage. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (exterior is free; interior entry ~€10) and the iconic Torre de Belém. The guided tour will provide rich historical context about Portugal's maritime empire and explorers like Vasco da Gama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Belém independently after the tour. Visit the free Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) exterior and the riverside promenade. Stop at the famous Pastéis de Belém bakery — the original home of the pastel de nata since 1837 — for just €1.50 per tart. Stroll along the waterfront back toward the city via tram or bus.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and visit the Miradouro de Santa Catarina (free viewpoint) for a stunning sunset over the Tagus River. This is a popular local hangout with street musicians and a relaxed vibe — bring a drink from a nearby minimarket to enjoy the view.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a quick café breakfast near your accommodation for €2–€4 before heading to Belém.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a picnic-style lunch near the Belém waterfront — pick up fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) for around €5–€7 total.
meals.dinner: Try a cervejaria (beer hall/seafood restaurant) in Cais do Sodré or Baixa for grilled sardines or amêijoas (clams). Many offer affordable set menus on Sundays. Budget €12–€15 including a beer or local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6 km west of central Lisbon — take Bus 727 or Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira (included in your Viva Viagem card credit). Sunday mornings are quieter in Belém, making it ideal for photos. The Pastéis de Belém queue moves quickly — don't be put off by the line.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Mouraria neighborhood — one of Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural districts, adjacent to Alfama. Visit the free Intendente Square and the beautiful Igreja de São Cristóvão. Wander through the historic streets where Fado music was born. Visit the free Fado Museum (Museu do Fado) in Alfama — entry is €5 and offers excellent insight into Portugal's soulful musical tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — entry is €5 and it is one of the most unique and underrated museums in Lisbon. Discover the history of Portugal's iconic azulejo tiles across stunning convent galleries. Afterward, explore the nearby Santa Apolónia area along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a live Fado performance — look for free or low-cost Fado ao Centro sessions at local tascas in Alfama or Mouraria. Some restaurants offer Fado with dinner for a minimum spend (~€15–€20), which is excellent value for an authentic cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Visit the Mercado de Campo de Ourique or a local café for a classic Portuguese breakfast — coffee and a croissant or pastel de nata for €2–€3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant in Mouraria for a hearty prato do dia. Try caldo verde (green soup) followed by a grilled meat or fish dish for €8–€11 including a drink.
meals.dinner: Combine dinner and Fado at a traditional Alfama tasca. Order house wine, bread, and a simple main course while enjoying live Fado music. Budget €15–€20 for the full experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Museu do Fado and Museu Nacional do Azulejo are both free on the first Sunday of each month — if timing aligns, plan accordingly. Monday can be a quiet day at museums, which is ideal for a relaxed visit. Always check opening hours in advance as some smaller venues close on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market in Campo de Santa Clara — open Tuesday and Saturday mornings. Browse vintage items, antiques, local crafts, and curiosities. This is a beloved local tradition and completely free to explore. Great for picking up affordable souvenirs like vintage tiles, old postcards, or Portuguese ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic ride on the historic Tram 28E through Alfama, Graça, and Estrela neighborhoods — a budget-friendly way to see the city (€3 with Viva Viagem card). Hop off at the Basílica da Estrela (free entry) and the nearby Jardim da Estrela park for a peaceful afternoon stroll among locals.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in the Príncipe Real neighborhood — an elegant, leafy area with independent boutiques, wine bars, and charming squares. Raise a final toast to Lisbon with a glass of local wine at a terrace bar and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Feira da Ladra market area — street vendors sell coffee and pastries for €1–€2.
meals.lunch: Eat near the Estrela/Príncipe Real area at a local tasca or grab a fresh sandwich from a padaria. Budget €6–€10 for a satisfying and affordable meal.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent final dinner — try a petiscos (Portuguese tapas) restaurant in Príncipe Real where you can share several small plates. Budget €15–€20 per person including wine, making it a memorable but still budget-friendly farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Feira da Ladra runs from approximately 09:00–17:00 on Tuesdays and Saturdays — arrive before 10:00 for the best selection. Tram 28E is iconic but can be crowded; if the wait is long, Bus 737 covers a similar route. Pack light souvenirs in your luggage and keep receipts for any VAT refund eligibility on purchases over €50.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Blue Line, ~35 min) to Lisbon City Stay. Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a hotel map and neighborhood walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Baixa-Chiado district near the hotel. Visit Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) along the Tagus riverfront, walk up to Chiado for window shopping and people-watching, and ride the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic views over the city rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — head to the historic Alfama neighborhood for an intimate Fado music performance paired with a traditional Portuguese dinner (petiscos, bacalhau, and local wine). Book in advance; shows typically begin around 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a quick pastel de nata and espresso (bica) at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel — try A Cevicheria or a local tasca in Chiado for a soup, sandwich, or prato do dia (dish of the day) around €10–14.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience (traditional Portuguese multi-course dinner with wine, ~€45–65 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00, so the morning slot is reserved for travel and check-in. Keep the afternoon light to recover from travel. Pre-book the Fado experience well in advance as seats are limited.

day_by_day.morning: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Brunch — head to the LX Factory in Alcântara (10-min Uber or tram 15E from Chiado). Explore the vibrant Sunday market with artisan crafts, vintage finds, local produce, and street food stalls inside a beautifully repurposed 19th-century industrial complex. Arrive by 10:00 to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the nearby Belém district. Explore independently: visit the Torre de Belém (exterior and grounds), Mosteiro dos Jerónimos (UNESCO site), and the Monument to the Discoveries along the riverfront. Take your time soaking in Portugal's Age of Discovery heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon. Explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — browse independent boutiques and relax at a terrace bar. Enjoy a casual evening dinner at a local restaurant in Príncipe Real or Bairro Alto.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at LX Factory — try the famous brunch spread at Rio Maravilha or one of the market food stalls (avocado toast, eggs, fresh juice, ~€12–18).
meals.lunch: Pastel de Belém (the original custard tarts) at Pastéis de Belém bakery — a Lisbon institution. Pair with a coffee and light snack (~€5–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taberna da Rua das Flores or similar traditional tasca in Príncipe Real — seasonal petiscos, grilled fish, and house wine (~€20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is the best day for LX Factory market (open 10:00–19:00). Belém is about 6 km from the city center — tram 15E is scenic but slow; Uber is faster. Jerónimos Monastery may have queues; consider buying tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Exploration — take a tuk-tuk or taxi up to Castelo de São Jorge. Explore the medieval ramparts and towers with sweeping 360° views over Lisbon and the Tagus River. Spend about 90 minutes inside the castle grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into the Mouraria neighborhood — Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural quarter. Join a guided walking tour or explore independently: visit the Intendente Square, street art murals, and local spice shops. Continue into Alfama's narrow alleyways, stopping at the Miradouro de Santa Luzia viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré. Graze through stalls from Lisbon's top chefs: try fresh seafood, bifanas, ginjinha, and pastéis. A perfect way to sample the city's culinary diversity in one place.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee, croissant, and fresh orange juice (~€4–6). Try Café Nicola or Confeitaria Nacional in Baixa.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Mouraria — eat at a local tasca or multicultural eatery in the neighborhood (~€10–15). Try a prato do dia with soup, main, and drink.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Time Out Market — budget €20–35 per person grazing across multiple stalls. Don't miss a glass of vinho verde or a craft beer from Musa Brewery.

day_by_day.notes: São Jorge Castle opens at 09:00; arrive early on weekdays to avoid tour groups. The walk from the castle down through Mouraria and Alfama is hilly — wear comfortable shoes. Time Out Market is open until midnight, making it ideal for a relaxed evening.

day_by_day.morning: Guided Walking Tour of Belém Historic District — join a guided group tour of Belém for a deeper dive into the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, Torre de Belém, and the surrounding maritime heritage sites. A knowledgeable guide brings the Age of Discovery era to life (tours typically 2.5–3 hours, starting ~09:30 or 10:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, visit the MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) in Belém — a striking riverside contemporary museum with rotating exhibitions. Then take the scenic tram 15E or Uber back toward central Lisbon and explore the Avenida da Liberdade boulevard for a leisurely walk.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Bairro Alto neighborhood as it comes alive at night. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar (try Park Bar on top of a parking garage for incredible sunset views). Follow with dinner at a restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before heading to Belém (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Post-tour lunch in Belém at Solar dos Presuntos or a riverside café — grilled sardines, salad, and wine (~€15–22 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Bairro Alto at Taberna do Bairro or Zé da Mouraria — traditional Portuguese cuisine with a modern twist (~€25–35 per person including wine).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Belém guided tour in advance online. MAAT museum entry is ~€9. Park Bar (Bairro Alto) is free entry but can get crowded — arrive by 18:30 for sunset views. Tuesday evenings in Bairro Alto are lively but less hectic than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Intendente and Anjos neighborhoods — off-the-beaten-path areas beloved by locals. Visit the Mercado de Intendente, browse independent coffee shops, and admire the beautiful azulejo (tile) facades on buildings. Stop at the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Chiado and Baixa for last-minute exploration. Visit the Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop), pick up souvenirs at local shops (tinned fish, wine, ceramics), and enjoy a final stroll along the Tagus riverfront at Cais do Sodré.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special mid-range restaurant in Chiado or Príncipe Real — splurge slightly for the final night. Enjoy a leisurely Portuguese meal with great wine, ending the trip on a high note.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in Intendente or Anjos — try a galão (milky espresso), tosta mista, and fresh fruit (~€5–7).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Tile Museum or in Intendente — soup and sandwich at a local café (~€8–12).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cantinho do Avillez (chef José Avillez's casual bistro in Chiado) or Alma restaurant — modern Portuguese cuisine (~€35–50 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) is a must — allow 1.5 hours; entry ~€5. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance, especially for popular spots like Cantinho do Avillez. If departing the next morning, pack bags the night before and confirm any airport transfers.

Explore the grand Praça do Comércio waterfront square, admire the Rua Augusta Arch, and soak in your first views of the Tagus River. Stop into a traditional pastelaria for a welcome espresso and pastel de nata.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the flight or a light snack upon arrival at the hotel's welcome service
meals.lunch: Casual but refined first taste of Lisbon — head to Cervejaria Ramiro, a Lisbon institution renowned for its exceptional fresh seafood and cold Sagres beer, just minutes from the city center
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — traditional Portuguese multi-course dinner with wine at a premium Fado house in Alfama

day_by_day.notes: Flight TP arrives at 13:00 — allow approximately 45–60 minutes for disembarkation, customs, and baggage. Private transfer to hotel recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm Fado dinner reservation in advance as top venues book quickly. Smart casual attire suggested for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Exploration — Begin the day with a guided visit to the magnificent Castelo de São Jorge, the medieval Moorish fortress perched atop Lisbon's highest hill. Enjoy sweeping 360-degree panoramic views over the city's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Descend into the vibrant, multicultural Mouraria neighborhood — Lisbon's oldest district and the birthplace of Fado — exploring its atmospheric narrow lanes, colorful tiles, and hidden squares with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for a curated culinary deep-dive. A local food expert guides you through the market's finest stalls, sampling signature dishes from Lisbon's most celebrated chefs — from perfectly grilled bacalhau to gourmet petiscos, artisan cheeses, and local wines. A sensory celebration of Portugal's extraordinary food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Príncipe Real neighborhood for aperitivo hour — visit a rooftop bar such as Park Bar (atop a multi-story car park) for sunset cocktails with sweeping city views. Follow with an elegant dinner at a Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the hotel or at Café A Brasileira in Chiado — one of Lisbon's most iconic literary cafés, famous for its gilded Art Nouveau interior and exceptional coffee
meals.lunch: Tastings included as part of the Time Out Market Food Tour experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, Michelin-starred) in Chiado — an exquisite celebration of modern Portuguese cuisine with impeccable service and an outstanding wine list

day_by_day.notes: São Jorge Castle opens at 09:00 — arriving early helps avoid midday crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the castle and Mouraria's cobblestone streets. Time Out Market is best experienced mid-afternoon when all stalls are fully operational. Book Alma restaurant well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Brunch — Spend a relaxed Sunday morning at the LX Factory, a beautifully repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara transformed into a vibrant creative hub. The legendary Sunday market fills its cobbled lanes with artisan crafts, vintage treasures, local design, books, and gourmet food stalls. Soak up the bohemian atmosphere, browse unique Portuguese goods, and enjoy a leisurely brunch at one of LX Factory's acclaimed restaurants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided Walking Tour of Belém Historic District — Just a short distance from LX Factory, dive into Lisbon's Age of Discovery heritage with an expert-guided walking tour of Belém. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline architecture, and the iconic Torre de Belém standing sentinel on the Tagus. Learn about Portugal's extraordinary 15th–16th century maritime empire and the explorers who changed the world. Stop at the original Pastéis de Belém bakery — the birthplace of the pastel de nata since 1837.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and enjoy a sunset Tuk-Tuk or classic yellow tram ride through Lisbon's scenic miradouros (viewpoints). End the day with a sophisticated dinner in the upscale Lapa or Santos district.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at LX Factory — dine at The Insólito or Cantina LX for a premium brunch spread featuring local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh pastries, eggs, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the café adjacent to Jerónimos Monastery, or a traditional lunch at Solar dos Presuntos near Belém — celebrated for its classic Portuguese recipes and exceptional regional wine cellar
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — a multi-concept premium dining experience celebrating the finest Portuguese ingredients with creative flair and theatrical presentation

day_by_day.notes: LX Factory Sunday Market runs from approximately 10:00–18:00 and is most lively in the morning. Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so Sunday is ideal. Belém is approximately 6 km from the city center — a scenic riverside taxi or Uber is recommended. Pre-book the Belém guided tour for a private premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of Lisbon's extraordinary azulejo (decorative tile) heritage. Begin at the Museu Nacional do Azulejo — housed in a stunning 16th-century convent — for an in-depth look at five centuries of Portuguese tile artistry, including the remarkable 23-meter panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon. Afterward, stroll through the Intendente and Graça neighborhoods discovering tile-adorned façades and hidden viewpoints favored by locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private food and wine tasting experience at a premium Lisbon wine bar or cellar specializing in Portuguese wines — explore exceptional Douro reds, Alentejo whites, and rare aged Colheita Ports with a sommelier guide. Follow with a leisurely walk through the elegant Avenida da Liberdade — Lisbon's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard — for premium shopping at flagship boutiques including Cartier, Louis Vuitton, and celebrated Portuguese leather and textile brands.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a luxury rooftop terrace — the SEEN Rooftop at Tivoli Avenida Liberdade or the Sky Bar at BLESS Hotel offer spectacular panoramic views over Lisbon's skyline and the Tagus. Conclude with a refined dinner celebrating Portuguese seafood at its finest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Nicolau Lisboa in Intendente — a beloved neighborhood café serving outstanding coffee, freshly baked pastries, and seasonal breakfast plates
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Taberna da Rua das Flores in Chiado — a celebrated petiscos restaurant showcasing the finest seasonal Portuguese ingredients in a warm, intimate setting with exceptional natural wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven Restaurant (Michelin-starred, Chef Joachim Koerper) overlooking Eduardo VII Park — refined contemporary cuisine with stunning panoramic city views and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Museu Nacional do Azulejo is located in the Xabregas district, a short taxi ride from the city center. Monday opening hours should be verified in advance. Wine tasting sessions can be arranged privately through the hotel concierge for the most personalized experience. Avenida da Liberdade boutiques generally open at 10:00.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel followed by a peaceful walk along the Tagus riverfront promenade (Ribeira das Naus). Browse the antique and book stalls along the river, pick up artisan Portuguese ceramics or ginjinha (cherry liqueur) as premium gifts at specialty shops in Baixa-Chiado. Visit the Livraria Bertrand in Chiado — the world's oldest operating bookshop (1732) — a wonderful final cultural stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if time permits, enjoy a final long, leisurely Portuguese lunch at a beloved traditional tasca. Afterward, private luxury transfer to Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport for departure. Pack any perishable food souvenirs (pastéis de nata, local cheeses, wines) in checked luggage.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the warmth of Lisbon's light, flavors, and Fado melodies with you as a lasting memory of this extraordinary city.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — request a premium spread with local cheeses, smoked ham, freshly squeezed orange juice, artisan breads, and pastel de nata
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at O Frade in Alfama or Tasca do Chico — intimate, beloved restaurants serving deeply traditional Portuguese home cooking with soulful character and outstanding regional wines
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport — Lisbon Airport's premium lounges offer a reasonable selection, but the true culinary highlight of the day is the farewell lunch

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport check-in procedures. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange the private airport transfer the evening before. Consider purchasing a curated selection of Portuguese wines, olive oils, or aged cheeses from a premium deli such as Conserveira de Lisboa or Garrafeira Nacional as final souvenirs.
